transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

I understand you've already cleaned the filter. To identify the correct part without guessing, I need to know if the pump is trying to work. Please run a drain-only cycle (or spin) and listen closely at the bottom front of the machine while it tries to empty. Do you hear a humming or buzzing noise from the pump area, or is it completely silent?
yeah it hums but the water doesn't move, no burning smell. there's a loud hum and a bit of a rattle. so is it the pump?

[Heading: Blocked or failing drain pump]
A loud hum with no water movement and a rattle strongly suggests the pump motor is trying to turn but can't—usually because something like a coin, button, or hair grip is jammed in the impeller, or the impeller itself has broken. Please unplug the machine first. Remove the filter again and shine a torch into the opening. Try turning the small plastic impeller (the fan-like part) gently with your finger or a non-metallic tool. Does it spin freely, is it stuck/jammed by something, or are the blades broken? This will tell us if we just need to clear a blockage or if the pump needs replacing.
ok did that, impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. also E18 came up on the display when it stalled. so is it the pump then?

[Heading: Blocked or damaged drain pump impeller]
Yes, the E18 code confirms a drainage fault, and your description of a loud hum with a rattle plus a stiff, gritty impeller points directly to the drain pump. The grit suggests debris is jamming the mechanism or the plastic blades are worn/broken, preventing it from moving water even though the motor is trying. Please ensure the machine is unplugged before attempting any replacement work. If you are comfortable with basic DIY, you can order a compatible drain pump for your Bosch model and replace it yourself. If not, this is a straightforward part swap that an engineer would perform.
ok but which pump exactly? all I've got is FD 9409 off the sticker inside the door, the E-Nr is rubbed off. is that enough to order one?

[Heading: Drain pump]
No, "FD 9409" is not enough to order the correct part. That looks like a model series or internal code, but Bosch requires the full Model number (e.g., WAX...) and specifically the E-Nr (or FNr) found on the rating plate inside the door frame to identify the exact pump variant. Since the E-Nr is rubbed off, you will need to remove the top cover of the machine to read the full model and E-Nr printed on a label there. Once you have those details, you can order the correct drain pump.
right, but I'm not taking the top off, I've no tools for that. is there any other way to get the right pump from what I've got? Bosch Serie 4, VarioPerfect on the front if that helps

[Heading: Drain pump failure requiring professional identification and replacement]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I understand you don't want to remove the top cover without tools. Unfortunately, "FD 9409" is an internal code and Bosch requires the full E-Nr (or FNr) on the rating plate to guarantee the correct drain pump fits. Since that label is inside the door frame but the main model/E-Nr plate is under the top lid, I cannot safely order the part for you without risking the wrong one arriving. Given your symptoms (humming, rattle, gritty impeller) and the E18 code, it is almost certainly a failed drain pump. Because you cannot access the rating plate to confirm the exact variant yourself, the best next step is to call an engineer. They can read the label once they open the machine and fit the correct part in one visit.
